rows.basis: Data Center market-platform revenue (10,613M of 26,914M total), the line treated as AI; it also includes non-AI data-center sales (e.g. cloud graphics, networking for general compute). Gaming, Professional Visualization, Automotive and OEM are excluded.
Data Center market-platform revenue (15,005M of 26,974M total), the line treated as AI; it includes some non-AI data-center sales. The MD&A's rounded $15.01B is the same figure.

Data Center market-platform revenue (47,525M of 60,922M total), kept as the series line. The MD&A estimates about 40% of Data Center revenue was for AI inference; that split is noted here, not used, because it is stated only for this year.

Data Center market-platform revenue (115,186M of 130,497M total), up 142%; MD&A attributes growth to Hopper for LLMs, recommenders and generative AI, and networking to Ethernet for AI. The line includes some non-AI data-center sales.

Data Center market-platform revenue (193,737M of 215,938M total), up 68%; this is the market line, not the Compute & Networking segment (193,479M), which includes automotive and pro-viz. Includes some non-AI data-center sales, and $4.6B of Q1 Hopper shipments to China.

No full-year Data Center outlook. Management cites visibility to nearly $20B of total CPU revenue this year, which is a product line rather than the Data Center series, and $1 trillion of Blackwell and Rubin revenue from 2025 through calendar 2027, a multi-year figure that cannot be assigned to FY2027. Neither is used as an amount.

The CFO says each GPU generation deployed at PORTS-Pike could represent about $150–200B of Nvidia revenue. That is per site and per generation, not a fiscal-year amount. Management also expects sequential growth to be driven primarily by Data Center.

No AI amount or share of Nvidia's own capex (976M) is stated; a chip seller's capex funds its buildings, labs and compute hardware, not the AI buildout. Seller-side signal: Data Center revenue 10,613M (fact:NVDA|segment_revenue|Data Center|FY2022).

No AI amount or share of capex (1,833M) is stated; the company's capex is its own facilities and equipment. Seller-side signal: Data Center revenue 15,005M (fact:NVDA|segment_revenue|Data Center|FY2023).
No AI amount or share of capex (1,069M) is stated. Seller-side signal: Data Center revenue 47,525M (fact:NVDA|segment_revenue|Data Center|FY2024).

No AI amount or share of capex (3,236M) is stated; growth in equipment and compute hardware PP&E is not split into internal AI clusters. Seller-side signal: Data Center revenue 115,186M (fact:NVDA|segment_revenue|Data Center|FY2025).

No AI amount or share of capex (6,042M) is stated. The $17.5B of private investments, the $13B Groq licence and the $5B Intel stake are investing flows or projects, not capex, and are excluded. Seller-side signal: Data Center revenue 193,737M (fact:NVDA|segment_revenue|Data Center|FY2026).
The MD&A says multi-year cloud service agreements entered in the second half of FY2023 support its AI cloud offerings and R&D; no amount or share of opex (11,132M) is attributed.
The earnings release expects the contracted cloud capacity to be used for NVIDIA AI cloud services and R&D; no amount is stated.

On the calls, total opex growth is guided to the upper-40s %, later the low-50s %, driven by R&D, product breadth and more use of AI tools. That guidance covers all opex; no AI amount or share is given.
